A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel CCIA with a multiple-chopping RRL and a pseudofeedback DSL that achieves a high noise efficiency factor with an ultra-low power consumption of 2.3 nW/Hz.

we have designed and fabricated a 2-μW, 45-nV/sqrtHz, 2.9-NeF, 0.23-mm2, 1.7-μA CCIA with a 0.18 μm CMOS process, which is the lowest power and smallest area among all the published results in the literature.
the proposed CCIA achieves an ultra-low-power and ultra-low-noise performance, and the DSL further improves the noise performance by 10 dB at low frequencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DSL and RRL can be combined to form a low-power and low-noise readout front end for neural recording applications, which is not possible with a conventional CCIA.
the proposed active high-pass filter in the RRL can reduce the capacitor size and the pseudofeedback DSL can achieve a subh-z corner while using only 15 pF of on-chip capacitance.
the DSL is a simple and effective way to achieve a high-pass corner of less than 1 Hz without the need for large capacitors.
